title: [Shai] Run the October developer survey (10 questions, team level)
what: Send a 10-question anonymous survey to R&D in October as the baseline: time saved, time lost and confidence when changing code.
why: Delivery metrics show what changed, not where time goes or how it feels. METR found developers felt faster while being slower, so we ask about time lost too and read it next to the metrics.
how: Build the Google Form from the questions file in the sketch. Don't collect emails; the only grouping field is team.
Send it in #engineering by 21 Oct with one line on why. Remind once after 3 days.
Report team level only, and fold any team with fewer than 5 answers into 'Other'.
Export the answers as CSV to a restricted Drive folder, and keep the questions file unchanged for December (G1-18).

title: [DevOps] Deploy the OTel Collector on inf with content scrubbing
needs: Sean fills the email → team map in Vault
what: Run an OpenTelemetry Collector on inf-rhinohealth as a Terraform helm_release unit. It takes OTLP in, drops content attributes, swaps the person's email for a team name, and writes metrics to VictoriaMetrics and events to VictoriaLogs.
why: Claude Code and the Agent SDK already export cost, tokens and tool decisions over OTel, but we have no collector. Scrubbing in one place means no prompt, command or file path is stored, even from a misconfigured client.
how: Create modules/otel-collector: a helm_release of the upstream open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector chart (contrib image, deployment mode, 2 replicas) plus an ExternalSecret from vault-store. Unit: multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/otel-collector/terragrunt.hcl.

Generate ingest_token and user_salt with Terraform into kvv2 infrastructure/otel-collector, like modules/n8n-secrets. Read the team map (work email → team) from infrastructure/ai-agents/teams with a vault_kv_secret_v2 data source and render it into the values template (sketch).

Drop prompt, prompt_text, user_system_prompt, full_command, file_path, tool_parameters and user.email before export. Keep user.hash (salted SHA-256), so weekly active users can be counted without names.

Ask for -opentelemetry.usePrometheusNaming=true on vminsert, so series get Prometheus names (claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total). Send logs to the long-term VictoriaLogs (1 year). No traces pipeline: there is no trace store yet.
Test from a pod with telemetrygen, then one real `claude -p` session with OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 set on purpose: the prompt must not show up in VictoriaLogs.

code.text:
mode: deployment
replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib   # contrib: transform processor and bearertokenauth
extraEnvsFrom:
  - secretRef: { name: otel-collector }              # ExternalSecret from kvv2 infrastructure/otel-collector
config:
  extensions:
    bearertokenauth: { token: "$${env:INGEST_TOKEN}" }
  receivers:
    otlp:
      protocols:
        http: { endpoint: "0.0.0.0:4318", auth: { authenticator: bearertokenauth } }
  processors:
    memory_limiter: { check_interval: 1s, limit_percentage: 80, spike_limit_percentage: 20 }
    transform/scrub:
      error_mode: ignore
      log_statements:
        - context: log      # metric_statements repeat this list with context: datapoint
          statements:
            - delete_matching_keys(attributes, "^(prompt|prompt_text|user_system_prompt|full_command|file_path|tool_parameters)$")
%{ for email, team in teams ~}
            - set(attributes["team"], "${team}") where attributes["user.email"] == "${email}"
%{ endfor ~}
            - set(attributes["user.hash"], SHA256(Concat([attributes["user.email"], "$${env:USER_SALT}"], ""))) where attributes["user.email"] != nil
            - delete_key(attributes, "user.email")
    batch: {}
  exporters:
    otlphttp/metrics: { metrics_endpoint: "${metrics_endpoint}" }   # vminsert .../insert/0/opentelemetry/v1/metrics
    otlphttp/logs: { logs_endpoint: "${logs_endpoint}" }            # vlsingle-rhino-logs-longterm:9428
  service:
    extensions: [bearertokenauth]
    pipelines:
      metrics: { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter, transform/scrub, batch], exporters: [otlphttp/metrics] }
      logs: { receivers: [otlp], processors: [memory_limiter, transform/scrub, batch], exporters: [otlphttp/logs] }

title: [Platform] Metrics job: pull fcp PRs nightly into VictoriaMetrics
needs: G3 creates RhinoHealth/ai-agents; decide the runner (no 'agents runner set' exists yet)
what: Start the nightly delivery-metrics job: a TypeScript workspace (`ai-agents/metrics`) that pulls fcp pull requests with their review timeline from GitHub and writes team-level series to VictoriaMetrics.
why: Review wait, lead time and change failure all start from the same PR data. We need it nightly, with a 12-week baseline before agents start, or we can't tell whether they helped.
how: Create the metrics workspace in RhinoHealth/ai-agents (`ai-agents/metrics/`, TypeScript on Node 24, global `fetch`): `src/github.ts` (sketch), `src/vm.ts` (writer), `src/teams.ts` (login → team from kvv2 infrastructure/ai-agents/teams), and a `delivery-metrics` bin (`src/cli.ts`) with `nightly` and `backfill --weeks 12`.
Read GitHub with a separate read-only App (pull requests, contents, actions, checks: read) through actions/create-github-app-token, so the rhino-ai-agents key stays with the broker alone.

Write Prometheus text with millisecond timestamps to the integration VMUser, the way infrastructure's send-workflow-result.yml does (Secrets Manager integration-metrics-user via the GitHubActions OIDC role; confirm it trusts RhinoHealth/ai-agents). Timestamps put backfilled points on the right days.

Workflow `ai-agents/.github/workflows/delivery-metrics.yml` on cron '20 2 * * *': actions/setup-node (24, npm cache), `npm ci --workspace metrics --include-workspace-root`, `npm run build -w shared -w metrics` (metrics imports the shared package), `node metrics/dist/cli.js nightly`. runs-on: an ai-agents runner set if G3 or G5 adds one by W3; until then ubuntu-22.04-2core, since the job only calls public APIs.
Aggregate before writing: series carry team, never login. Teams under 3 people report as 'other'.

Check the WAF doesn't block protobuf bodies; add a rule exception for these two paths if it does.

title: [Platform] Metrics job: compute delivery metrics, backfill 12 weeks
needs: G2 golden-set miner (bug → PR that introduced it); G2 live metrics (Byte's two rates); G3 run records (stuck loops, clean endings)

title: [Platform] Eval results store: JSON in S3, pass rates as metrics
needs: G3 ai-agents account and its GitHub OIDC role; suites from G2, G4, G5, G6 and G8 write through it
what: One place for every eval run: each suite writes one JSON file per run to an S3 bucket in the ai-agents account, and the nightly job turns new files into pass-rate, spread and cost series.
why: Five suites from five goals need one format, so a change can be judged on quality, cost, steps and time together. JSON plus Grafana is enough until Q1; Langfuse needs ClickHouse.
how: Bucket rhino-ai-agents-eval-results: one unit at terraform/accounts/ai-agents/aws/us-east-1/evals/results-bucket/terragrunt.hcl (tfr:///terraform-aws-modules/s3-bucket/aws 5.13.0, KMS, versioning, no public access). A person applies.

`ai-agents/evals/results.py` (sketch; it stays Python, next to Harbor and the suites that call it): suites call record(). Sandbox VMs write with their instance role through the S3 VPC endpoint, so no key sits in the VM.

The nightly metrics job (TypeScript, `ai-agents/metrics/src/eval-results.ts` with `@aws-sdk/client-s3`) reads new files with a read-only role in the ai-agents account (GitHub OIDC) and pushes ai_agents_eval_pass_rate, _pass_rate_spread, _cost_per_case_usd and _median_turns with suite, version, split, model and effort labels.
Schema rules: every case runs 3 times, and each run records pass, cost, turns, agents used, seconds and a cause label for failures.

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/results.py  (every suite calls record(); Python, like Harbor and the suites around it)
"""One JSON file per eval run. Quality, cost, steps, agents and time are scored together."""
import json
import statistics

import boto3

BUCKET = "rhino-ai-agents-eval-results"
CAUSES = {"too_many_tools", "bad_handoff", "contradicting_prompt", "missing_context", "flaky_environment"}


def record(suite: str, version: str, setup: dict, cases: list[dict], started_at: str) -> str:
    """setup: {"split": "dev", "model": "claude-opus-5-5", "effort": "medium", "harness": "0.4.1"}
    cases: [{"id": "T-017", "runs": [{"pass": True, "cost_usd": 1.9, "turns": 41, "agents": 3,
                                       "seconds": 820, "cause": None}, ...]}]   # 3 runs per case"""
    assert all(len(case["runs"]) == 3 for case in cases), "every case runs 3 times"
    runs = [run for case in cases for run in case["runs"]]
    assert all(run["cause"] in CAUSES for run in runs if not run["pass"]), "label every failure"
    per_round = [statistics.mean(case["runs"][i]["pass"] for case in cases) for i in range(3)]
    summary = {
        "pass_rate": statistics.mean(per_round),
        "pass_rate_spread": max(per_round) - min(per_round),  # small suites swing a lot; always show it
        "cost_per_case_usd": sum(run["cost_usd"] for run in runs) / len(runs),
        "median_turns": statistics.median(run["turns"] for run in runs),
    }
    key = f"{suite}/{version}/{setup['split']}/{started_at}.json"
    body = {"suite": suite, "version": version, "setup": setup, "summary": summary, "cases": cases}
    boto3.client("s3").put_object(Bucket=BUCKET, Key=key, Body=json.dumps(body).encode())
    return key  # the nightly job turns new keys into ai_agents_eval_<summary field> series

title: [Platform] Grafana: agent operations dashboard
what: A Grafana dashboard for running agents: cost and tokens per agent, cache-read share, API errors and rejected tool calls.
why: This is the screen we open when something feels off, and in the weekly run review. It shows agents, never people.
how: Add modules/grafana/dashboards/AI-Agents/ai-agents-operations.json in infrastructure. The sidecar loads every JSON file there, and the folder name becomes the Grafana folder.
Cost and tokens come from the gateway series. People's Claude Code series are not on this dashboard.
Errors and rejected tools come from Claude Code events in VictoriaLogs (api_error, tool_decision with decision reject), per agent.
Cache-read share under 70% turns red: something is breaking the prompt cache (a model switch, a changing tool list, a timestamp in the prompt).
Check the exact series and field names in vmui and VictoriaLogs first; Prometheus naming adds unit and _total suffixes.

{
  "title": "AI agents: operations",
  "uid": "ai-agents-ops",
  "tags": ["ai-agents"],
  "time": { "from": "now-7d", "to": "now" },
  "templating": { "list": [ {
    "name": "agent", "type": "query", "multi": true, "includeAll": true,

    "query": "label_values(ai_agents_llm_cost_usd_total, agent)" } ] },

      "targets": [ { "expr": "sum(rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type=\"cache_read\",agent=~\"$agent\"}[6h])) / sum(rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type=~\"input|cache_read|cache_write\",agent=~\"$agent\"}[6h]))" } ] },

title: [Platform] Grafana spend view and a burn-rate alert for Sean and Nir
needs: G0 spend-limits.yaml for the monthly budget
what: A spend dashboard with team totals, spend per agent, cost per ticket and per merged PR, and cache-read share, plus a daily check that alerts Sean and Nir when the month runs more than 25% ahead of budget.
why: We control tokens with visibility first. The forecast catches a bad month while there is time to act, and it never stops anything.
how: Add AI-Agents/ai-spend.json: people's spend by team (claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total by team), agent spend by agent (gateway), cost per ticket (gateway series by jira), and cost per merged agent PR (merged PR keys from G1-07).
No panel has a person dimension. Each person sees their own spend in /usage and the status line only.
The nightly job writes ai_spend_mtd_usd and ai_spend_budget_usd (from spend-limits.yaml) per scope: people, and each agent.
Add the rules in the sketch and route them to #ai-agents-alerts, mentioning Sean and Nir, with what drives the spend (the top 3 teams or agents by week-over-week growth).

code.text:
# infrastructure/multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/victoria-metrics/alerting/templates/alert_rules/ai-spend.yml
---

- name: ai-spend
  interval: 1h
  rules:
    - alert: AISpendAheadOfBudget
      # Month-to-date spend more than 25% ahead of a straight line to the monthly budget.
      expr: |-
        sum by (scope) (ai_spend_mtd_usd)
          > 1.25 * sum by (scope) (ai_spend_budget_usd) * day_of_month() / days_in_month()
      for: 6h
      labels:
        severity: warning
        cloud.account.name: inf
        service.name: ai-agents
        service.component: spend
      annotations:
        summary: "[AI spend «{{ $labels.scope }}»] month-to-date is more than 25% ahead of budget"
        description: "An alert, never a stop. The AI spend dashboard shows which teams or agents drive it."
        external_link: "https://grafana.example.com/d/ai-spend"
    - alert: AICacheReadShareLow
      expr: |-
        sum by (agent) (rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type="cache_read"}[6h]))
          / sum by (agent) (rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type=~"input|cache_read|cache_write"}[6h])) < 0.70
      for: 2h
      labels:
        severity: warning
        cloud.account.name: inf
        service.name: ai-agents
        service.component: spend
      annotations:
        summary: "[AI agent «{{ $labels.agent }}»] reads under 70% of its input from the prompt cache"

  ]
}

title: [Platform] DX's three lenses side by side: utilization, impact, cost
needs: G4 plan step records the human-equivalent hours
what: Compute and show DX's three lenses side by side, team level only: utilization (weekly AI users, share of PRs with AI help, tasks given to agents), impact (merged PRs next to change failure, human-equivalent hours of agent work) and cost (AI spend total and per engineer, agent cost per human-equivalent hour).
why: Any one lens alone misleads: usage can rise while impact falls, and impact can rise at a cost we don't want. DX's framework reads them together.
how: Add `src/lenses.ts` (sketch) to the nightly job and write delivery_lens_* series per team and week.

Weekly AI users: distinct user.hash in Claude Code metrics. Share of PRs with AI help: Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers or 'Generated with Claude Code' in the body. Tasks given to agents: Jira tickets assigned to Nova plus routine runs.
Human-equivalent hours: decide with Nir. Proposal: Nova's plan states how long an engineer would need, and the plan approver confirms or corrects it.
The plan writes the agent hourly rate as 'hours ÷ cost'; as a rate it is cost ÷ hours. Show dollars per human-equivalent hour and confirm the wording with Nir.
Add a 'Three lenses' row at the top of delivery-impact.json, the three side by side over the same weeks.

title: [Platform] Step tracing: tag every run by step and harness version
needs: G3 harness (nova-worker) and G3 workflows; G0 gateway reads the step header
what: Every OTel signal, gateway call and Temporal activity of a run carries the same tags: agent, Jira key, run, one of the nine steps, and the harness version.
why: When a run goes wrong we need to see which step spent the tokens and which step should have caught the problem. That needs every signal tagged the same way.
how: Add `ai-agents/harness/src/telemetry.ts` (sketch): one env per Agent SDK session, passed as `options.env` to `query()` on top of `process.env` (the option replaces the environment, so spread it). Each step is its own session, so the resource attributes stay right.
The gateway already reads x-ai-agents-step; check its token and cost series carry the step label.
Set Temporal search attributes Step and HarnessVersion (`upsertSearchAttributes` with typed keys from `defineSearchAttributeKey`), so the Temporal UI filters the same way.
harness.version comes from harness/package.json's version and changes on every harness release, so evals and live runs can be split by it.
Check one dogfood run end to end: cost by step in Grafana adds up to the run's gateway total.

title: [Platform] Label failed runs with the step that should have caught them
what: A small command for the weekly run review that labels each failed or rejected run with where it failed, the step that should have caught it, and a cause.
why: A problem seen twice should become a check, a lint rule or a skill line. That only happens if failures are labelled the same way every week.
how: Add `ai-agents/harness/src/label-run.ts` (sketch), run from an ai-agents checkout as `npx tsx harness/src/label-run.ts <run-id> --failed-at … --should-have-caught … --cause …`. It writes runs/<run>/label.json to the eval results bucket.
Steps are the nine from the quality table; causes are the five eval cause labels plus 'model' and 'unknown'.
The nightly job counts labels into ai_agents_run_failures_total{failed_at, should_have_caught, cause}; add a panel to the operations dashboard.
Use it in the weekly 30-minute run review of 5 traces (2 at random, the 3 worst). A label seen twice in a month gets a ticket.

title: [Platform] Nightly quality numbers for each step of a Nova run
needs: G4 readiness check, plan step and self-review receipt; G2 Byte findings
what: Add the step-quality numbers to the nightly job: ready on first try, plan adherence, first-pass green, caught before the PR, and approvals faster than 60 seconds flagged.
why: Each step has one gate and one number. These show which gate is weak before the end result does.
how: Read run records from Temporal and the run JSON in S3; read Byte's findings from G2's live metrics.
Write per agent and week: delivery_ready_first_try_ratio, delivery_plan_unplanned_files, delivery_plan_items_not_done, delivery_first_pass_green_ratio, delivery_caught_before_pr_ratio.
Fast approvals are a list, not a score: post the run links of plan or PR approvals under 60 s to the weekly review thread. They flag the run, never rank a person.
Add a 'Quality at every step' row to the delivery-impact dashboard.

title: [Platform] Effort sweep: confirm the routing table on our code
needs: G2 BYTE-GOLD dev split, G4 TICKET-BENCH smoke, G3 routing table in the harness
what: Before real pilot tickets, run a small effort sweep on TICKET-BENCH and BYTE-GOLD that tries each routing table row one level up and one level down.
why: Most routing numbers are Anthropic's, not ours. A row that loses quality on our code goes one level up, and a cheaper setting stays only while its slice holds.
how: Write the sweep file (sketch) and run it on wide sandbox VMs; results land in the eval store.
Each setting runs 3 times. A cheaper setting passes when its pass rate is within the current setting's spread.
Effort changes per message, not per session, so the prompt cache stays warm.
Update the harness routing table in one PR that links the scoreboard; a person approves it.

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/sweeps/2026-w9-effort.yaml
# Confirms the routing table on our code before real pilot tickets. Results go to the eval store.
vm_size: wide
repeats: 3                          # report the spread, never a single run
suites:
  ticket-bench: { split: smoke }    # 15 tasks (G4)
  byte-gold:    { split: dev }      # never the holdout (G2)
rows:                               # the table's current setting first, then one level each side
  - job: build_typical
    suite: ticket-bench
    settings: [opus-5-5/medium, opus-5-5/low, opus-5-5/high]
  - job: build_hard
    suite: ticket-bench
    settings: [opus-5-5/high, opus-5-5/medium, opus-5-5/xhigh]
  - job: review_logic_security
    suite: byte-gold
    settings: [opus-5-5/medium, opus-5-5/low, opus-5-5/high]
  - job: review_conventions
    suite: byte-gold
    settings: [sonnet-5-5/low, sonnet-5-5/medium, opus-5-5/low]
effort_changes: per message         # keeps the prompt cache warm
decision:
  keep_cheaper_if: its pass_rate >= current pass_rate - current spread
  if_a_row_loses_quality: move that row one level up
  apply_as: one harness PR that links the scoreboard; a person approves it

title: [Shai] Repeat the developer survey in December and compare
what: Send the same 10 questions in December and compare with October, team level, with ranges.
why: The December survey says whether people's time and confidence moved, next to what the metrics say.
how: Rebuild the form from the unchanged questions.yaml and send it by 10 Dec with the same wording.
From an ai-agents checkout (after `npm ci`), run `npx tsx metrics/src/survey-compare.ts october.csv december.csv` (sketch) on the two CSV exports. Teams under 5 answers fold into 'Other'.
Put it next to the delivery-impact numbers in the quarter report: both directions, with ranges, no per-person view.

title: [Platform] New-model check: rerun suites with and without each harness part
needs: G3 harness flags that switch parts off
what: A repeatable check for every new model: run each suite on the new model with and without each harness part, and move a setting only if its slice holds.
why: Anthropic dropped a whole harness step when a newer model no longer needed it. Parts that stopped helping cost tokens and slow runs.
how: Add `ai-agents/evals/sweeps/new-model.yaml` (sketch) listing the harness parts that can be switched off.
Run it once in W12 on the current model as the reference, so the next model release has a baseline.
A part goes only when removing it keeps the pass rate within the spread and lowers cost or time; that change goes into the monthly rule-diet PR.

code.text:
# ai-agents/evals/sweeps/new-model.yaml
# Run when a new model ships, and once in W12 on today's model as the reference.
model_under_test: claude-opus-5-5         # replace with the new model's ID
reference: { model: claude-opus-5-5, harness: current }
repeats: 3
suites: [ticket-bench/smoke, byte-gold/dev, routine-bench/weekly, skill-evals/nightly, brain-qa/nightly]
harness_parts:                            # each one is switched off alone; all others stay on
  - self_review_subagent
  - qa_agent
  - scope_judge
  - progress_watcher_nudges
  - plan_grill
  - kb_skill
runs:
  - { name: full, model: "{model_under_test}", parts_off: [] }
  - { name: without-each-part, model: "{model_under_test}", parts_off: each }
decision:
  move_model_if: every suite's pass_rate >= reference pass_rate - spread, and cost per case doesn't rise
  drop_part_if: pass_rate stays within the spread without it, and cost or time falls
  apply_as: the monthly rule-diet PR; a person approves it
